name: Monport GT 60W MOPA Fiber
tagline: 60W Split fiber laser engraver with autofocus from Monport
tldr: Monport GT 60W MOPA Fiber is the 60W SKU on the Monport monport gt line. Monport GT 30W brings split-cabinet fiber marking with autofocus: useful for varying part heights. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Maximum fiber marking speed and depth in the line

priceRange.note: Official Monport store, Oct 2026: $3,600 to $4,950 depending on manual-focus fiber or autofocus MOPA

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

pros: MOPA pulse control (2–500 ns, 1–3,000 kHz): colour marking on stainless and cleaner marks on plastics
Least expensive colour-capable model in the GT line at $4,699.99 (Monport, Oct 2026)
Short pulses help white or black marks on anodized aluminum and limit heat on thin parts
cons: About $1,100 more than the GT 50W for the same 0.10 mm listed marking depth
175 × 175 mm field, smaller than the GT 50W's 200 × 200 mm
Colour marking takes time on test grids: settings are not plug-and-play

faq.question: Can the GT 60W MOPA do colour marking on stainless steel?
faq.answer: Yes. It is the entry point for colour in the GT series: the MOPA source adjusts pulse width from 2 to 500 ns and frequency from 1 to 3,000 kHz, which is what controlled oxide colours on stainless and titanium require. Expect to build your own colour test grids, since results depend on alloy, surface finish and speed.

faq.question: How deep does the GT 60W engrave, and how fast?
faq.answer: Monport lists the same 0.10 mm maximum marking depth as the GT 50W, with 1.5 mJ pulse energy and a 10,000 mm/s top speed. In our benchmark, a filled 10 × 10 cm logo on stainless takes about 3–7 minutes. Deeper relief needs repeated passes.

faq.question: GT 60W MOPA or GT 100W MOPA?
faq.answer: At $4,699.99 (Monport, October 2026) the 60W costs about $1,900 less than the GT 100W ($6,600 pre-order). Both share the pulse range, colour capability and 175 × 175 mm field. Choose the 100W if deep engraving (0.15 mm listed vs 0.10 mm) or cutting throughput pays your bills; for colour, plastics and black marking, the 60W covers it.

standoutFeatures.title: Entry to colour marking
standoutFeatures.body: The GT 60W is the least expensive GT with a MOPA source. Adjustable 2–500 ns pulses open colour on stainless, white or black marks on anodized aluminum and gentler marking on plastics.

standoutFeatures.title: Wide frequency range
standoutFeatures.body: 1–3,000 kHz, against 20–80 kHz on the GT 50W. High frequencies with short pulses give smooth surface finishes; lower frequencies with longer pulses favour depth.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 60W SKU on Monport GT MOPA Fiber. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Push speed only after depth tests on your metal alloy. Cooling and lens cleanliness matter more at this power level.
primaryUse: High-power fiber for metal-focused shops needing line-top throughput

editorialDepth.advantages: Monport GT MOPA Fiber 60W fits shops that mark stainless, aluminum, and tools daily without a CO₂ bay. A solid bench option for jewelry, tags, and small batches.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if wood, leather, or cast acrylic pay your bills. Deep metal cutting and large industrial panels often need more fiber headroom (100W) or a different machine class.
